question: With a policy whose filesystem.readwritePaths is a tree T and whose filesystem.deniedPaths is a subtree T/sub inside it, do write attempts from inside the container into T/sub fail, while writes inside T but outside T/sub succeed? Judged for the Microsoft-signed wxc-exec v1.0.0 launcher on the tier this build selects.

hardware.note: hardware description from the host record; the raw batch header does not carry it. No GPU or model work.

windows.note: ProductName is read from the registry as written by Windows; the build number is 26200 (Windows 11 family).

summary: Tier 1 (base-container) with native deny advertised: in 3 of 3 launched runs every one of 5 write attempts into T/sub (create a file, open the marker for append, rename a file, delete a file, create a directory) was refused with Win32 error 5, 15 of 15 attempts; the host-side comparison of T/sub before and after found no change in any run; writes inside T outside T/sub landed in 3 of 3 runs; a read of the marker and a listing of T/sub from inside the container were also refused with error 5 (3 of 3 each); the same 5 attempts from an unconfined process on the same account landed (1 run, 5 of 5). icacls captures of T/sub before, during and after each run were identical and held 5 inherited allow entries and no deny entry. Harness verdict HOLD.

v100.authenticode: Valid|CN=Microsoft Corporation, O=Microsoft Corporation, L=Redmond, S=Washington, C=US

main.note: Probed only (S0). The sha256 equals the main-build launcher of the loopback-proxy record of the same day, which that record states was built from microsoft/mxc commit 525d0f25763b2edaab56e29651fb7c12c4cbbd93; this batch's raw header does not record a commit.

harness.reviews: five pre-run rounds (FAIL, FAIL, PASS, FAIL, PASS)
harness.approved_by: an independent non-elevated reviewer after round 5, 2026-10-15T22:30:40Z; launch.ps1 refuses to run unless every script's sha256 is in the approved list
harness.line_endings_note: The committed blobs are LF; the approved hashes are of the working-copy bytes that ran (CRLF for seven files, LF for smoke_payload.py). The evidence copy holds those bytes.
harness.self_test_closing_tally: 167 passed, 0 failed (round 5 addendum, quiet machine); not run during or after the live batch

policy.tree_root: C:\mxc-fx (the harness's TREE_ROOT constant), a fresh tree per run, removed after the launch
policy.allowDaclMutation: not present in the submitted policy (the launcher's default; resolved `true` in the launcher's log)
policy.ui_lockdown_note: UI lockdown is off (ui.disable false, clipboard none, injection false): with it on, importing _ctypes fails inside the container; this probe measures the filesystem only

machine.launching_account: the operator's own account (name not recorded here)
machine.note: Bitdefender present. Its absence was not measured for this case. The stale McAfee Security Center entry is as in the loopback-proxy record.

results.launcher_captureDenials_note: Reported by the launcher on stderr of each launch (the learning-mode trace; accesses still denied). The number 9 per run was not reconciled with the 7 refused operations the payload recorded (5 write attempts, 2 reads) and is recorded as observed.

acl_captures.tool: icacls and the security descriptor (SDDL) of T/sub and of T, captured by the harness on the host
acl_captures.reading: On this tier the deny was not implemented with a host DENY ACE on T/sub: no deny entry appeared before, during or after any run, and the entries were unchanged. The records say nothing about how the OS enforced the deny.

launcher_log_facts.psec_note: Every one of the 4 launches (3 measured runs and the smoke launch) logged: process security environment spec built (PSEC 1.0, 312 bytes). The text is in the launcher's own log with interleaved timestamp prefixes; strip them to read it. --probe prints no PSEC field. The logged PSEC version is a per-launch reading of the policy launched, never a property of the host.

non_results.what_happened: The container's Python failed at 'import ctypes' with 'ImportError: DLL load failed while importing _ctypes: A dynamic link library initialization routine failed' (the policy then had ui.disable true). No container report was produced and nothing was written to T/sub; the only counted landing in that batch is the unconfined control (5 of 5 landed). The harness then gained a smoke launch of the container's Python and ran with ui.disable false, clipboard none, injection false; the smoke launch imported ctypes. The harness changed between the two batches as well as the UI setting, so the UI setting is the recorded difference and not an isolated cause.

not_measured: Tier 2/3 (AppContainer, host DENY ACE enforcement): this build selected Tier 1, so the mechanism the vendor documents for those tiers was not exercised; nothing here is a statement about them
any build other than the signed v1.0.0 launcher for the measured runs (the main-build launcher was probed only)
a machine without Bitdefender (it was present; its absence was not measured for this case)
a non-elevated launch (the batch was launched elevated)
UI lockdown on (ui.disable true): with it on, the container's Python could not load ctypes in the first attempt
moving a file into T/sub; renaming T/sub itself; writes to alternate data streams; other path spellings (8.3 names, letter case, trailing dot, long-path prefixes)
a denied path that is a reparse point, junction or symlink, or on another volume
per-entry ACL changes, timestamp-only changes and the archive bit inside T/sub (host comparison covers names, sizes, hashes, attributes, file write times and alternate data streams)
the fx-b variant with allowDaclMutation false (S5): applies only on Tier 2/3 and was not run
the enumeratePaths field; captureDenials mode allow; concurrent runs sharing a containerId
the session-isolation and WSLc backends; nono under MXC; anything about any fork
variance beyond three runs on one machine within about eight seconds (a repeat, not a distribution)
how the OS enforced the deny on Tier 1 (the launcher's log and the vendor documentation describe native enforcement; no kernel-level evidence was taken here)
